inputs.task:
Review this native send preparation used by a JDK 22 FFM service on Linux 6.6 with liburing 2.5. The protocol requires all 8192 bytes of record A to precede the 4096 bytes of record B on one TCP connection. Slow receivers are part of the supported workload.

Read native_send.c and send_policy.c. Decide whether the prepared pair preserves that byte order when progress is partial. If a change is needed, make the smallest supported correction to these files; otherwise retain them and explain why. Write review.md with the decision, the relevant runtime contract, and the validation still needed before rollout.

Fixture facts: both SQEs are obtained and submitted together as one batch; there are no other sends on this connection. The surrounding dispatcher handles every CQE by stable user_data, tracks actual byte counts, retains SEND_ZC buffers through any required NOTIF, observes canceled requests, and enforces a per-connection byte budget and deadline. It can retry remaining bytes after a partial completion but cannot retract bytes that a dependent request has already sent. Do not redesign those existing ownership controls or silently upgrade the baseline.

These are development review fragments, not an executable service. Do not claim a Linux runtime test from static review.

sources.supports: Linked SEND_ZC requires MSG_WAITALL in send flags when short send must count as link failure.
The same linked-send precondition applies to ordinary SEND.

io_send/io_send_zc initialize min_ret to zero and require MSG_WAITALL to set a full-length threshold; retryable partials accumulate done_io; terminal failure can return accumulated positive bytes while marking failure.
io_req_find_next processes link failure state and otherwise queues the successor; source review corroborates the interleaving risk inferred for a positive short SEND without the flag.
io_uring_prep_send and io_uring_prep_send_zc assign the flags argument to sqe->msg_flags; SEND_ZC zc_flags goes to ioprio, separate from generic SQE flags.
